'''Noga M. Alon''' ({{langx|he|נוגה אלון}}; born 1956) is an Israeli [[mathematician]]. He is professor emeritus at [[Tel Aviv University]] and a professor of mathematics at [[Princeton University]] noted for his contributions to [[combinatorics]] and [[theoretical computer science]], having authored hundreds of papers.

== Education and career ==
Alon was born in 1956 in [[Haifa]], where he graduated from the [[Hebrew Reali School]] in 1974. He graduated [[summa cum laude]] from the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]] in 1979, earned a master's degree in mathematics in 1980 from [[Tel Aviv University]],<ref name=cv/> and received his Ph.D. in Mathematics at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1983 with the dissertation ''Extremal Problems in Combinatorics'' supervised by [[Micha Perles]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=58918}}</ref>

After postdoctoral research at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], Alon returned to Tel Aviv University as a senior lecturer in 1985, obtained a permanent position as an associate professor there in 1986, and was promoted to full professor in 1988. He was head of the School of Mathematical Science from 1999 to 2001, and was awarded the Florence and Ted Baumritter Combinatorics and Computer Science Chair.<ref name=cv>{{cite web <!-- Citation bot bypass-->|url=https://www.ae-info.org/attach/User/Alon_Noga/CV/Alon_Noga_cv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref> He retired as professor emeritus from Tel Aviv and became a professor at [[Princeton University]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.math.princeton.edu/~nalon/cvshort.html|title=Short CV|publisher=Princeton University|access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref>

He was editor-in-chief of the journal ''Random Structures and Algorithms'' from 2008 through 2023.<ref name=ae/>

== Research ==
Alon has published more than five hundred research papers, mostly in [[combinatorics]] and in [[theoretical computer science]], and one book, on the [[probabilistic method]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Alon |first=Noga |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9780470277331 |title=The Probabilistic Method |last2=Spencer |first2=Joel H. |date=2008-07-25 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-0-470-17020-5 |language=en |doi=10.1002/9780470277331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=List of publications and papers available on-line |url=https://www.cs.tau.ac.il//~nogaa/PDFS/publications.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250109070226/https://www.cs.tau.ac.il//~nogaa/PDFS/publications.html |archive-date=2025-01-09 |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=www.cs.tau.ac.il |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> He has also published under the pseudonym "A. Nilli", based on the name of his daughter Nilli Alon.<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Ceccherini-Silberstein | first1 = Tullio
 | last2 = Scarabotti | first2 = Fabio
 | last3 = Tolli | first3 = Filippo
 | doi = 10.1017/9781316856383
 | isbn = 978-1-107-18233-2
 | mr = 3791831
 | page = 300
 | publisher = Cambridge University Press, Cambridge
 | series = Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics
 | title = Discrete Harmonic Analysis: Representations, Number Theory, Expanders, and the Fourier Transform
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=HYRnDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA300
 | volume = 172
 | year = 2018| s2cid = 125447782
 }}</ref>

His research contributions include the [[Restricted sumset#Combinatorial Nullstellensatz|combinatorial Nullstellensatz]], an algebraic tool with applications in combinatorics; [[color-coding]], a technique for [[parameterized complexity|fixed-parameter tractability]] of pattern-matching algorithms in graphs; and the [[Alon–Boppana bound]] in [[spectral graph theory]].

== Awards ==
Alon has received a number of awards, including the following:
* 1989 – [[Erdős Prize]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/Anna_and_Lajos_Erdos_Prize/|title=The Anna and Lajos Erdős Prize in Mathematics|work=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive|access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>
* 2000 – [[George Pólya Prize]] in Applied Combinatorics of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/major-prizes-lectures/detail/george-polya-prize-applied-combinatorics|title=George Pólya Prize in Applied Combinatorics|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|work=Major Prizes & Lectures|access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>
* 2001 – Michael Bruno Memorial Award of the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iias.huji.ac.il/brunolaureates|title=Bruno Laureates|website=iias.huji.ac.il}}</ref>
* 2005 – [[Gödel Prize]], with [[Yossi Matias]] and [[Mario Szegedy]], for their paper "The space complexity of approximating the frequency moments" on [[streaming algorithm]]s<ref>{{cite web|publisher=European Association for Theoretical Computer Science|title=Gödel Prize – 2005|url=https://eatcs.org/index.php/component/content/article/503|access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref>
* 2008 – [[Israel Prize]], for mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web| title = Israel Prize Official Site (in Hebrew) – Recipient's C.V. | url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsah/NogaAlon/CvNohaAlon.htm }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title = Israel Prize Official Site (in Hebrew) – Judges' Rationale for Grant to Recipient | url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashsah/NogaAlon/NsNogaAlon.htm}}</ref>
* 2011 – [[EMET Prize]], with [[Saharon Shelah]], for mathematics.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.haaretz.com/2011-11-21/ty-article/news-in-brief/0000017f-e198-d804-ad7f-f1fafd710000|department=News in brief|title=Haaretz photographer Miki Kratsman among new recipients of Emet Prize|date=21 November 2011|newspaper=Haaretz|access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref>
* 2019 – [[Paris Kanellakis Award]], with [[Phillip Gibbons]], [[Yossi Matias]] and [[Mario Szegedy]], "for foundational work on streaming algorithms and their application to large scale data analytics"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://awards.acm.org/award-recipients/alon_6955744|title=Noga Alon|work=Award recipients|publisher=Association for Computing Machinery|access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref>
* 2021 – [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Mathematical Exposition, with [[Joel Spencer]], for ''The Probabilistic Method''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6484|title=News from the AMS|website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>
* 2022 – [[Shaw Prize]] in Mathematical Sciences, with [[Ehud Hrushovski]], "for their remarkable contributions to discrete mathematics and model theory with interaction notably with algebraic geometry, topology and computer sciences"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.shawprize.org/prizes/mathematical-sciences|title=The Shaw Prize|website=www.shawprize.org}}</ref>
* 2022 – [[Knuth Prize]], "for foundational contributions in combinatorics and graph theory and applications to fundamental topics in computer science"<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Knuth Prize Awarded to Noga Alon |url=https://www.sigact.org/prizes/knuth/citation2022.pdf |access-date=July 2, 2022 |website=ACM Special Interest Group on Algorithms and Computation Theory}}</ref>
* 2024 – [[Wolf Prize in Mathematics]] "for his fundamental contributions to Combinatorics and Theoretical Computer Science”.{{Citation needed|date=August 2025}}

Alon gave plenary addresses at the 1996 [[European Congress of Mathematics]], at the 2002 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]],<ref name=ae/> at the 2009 Turán Memorial Lectures,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://old.renyi.hu/turanlectures_vk.html|title=Paul Turán Memorial Lectures|website=old.renyi.hu}}</ref> and a lecture in the 1990 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref name=ae/> In 2015 he gave the [[Łojasiewicz Lecture]] (on the "Signrank and its applications in combinatorics and complexity") at the [[Jagiellonian University|Jagiellonian University in Kraków]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://im.uj.edu.pl/en_GB/lojasiewicz/2015|title=S.Lojasiewicz Lecture 2015|publisher=Institute of Mathematics of the Jagiellonian University|access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref> He was given an [[honorary doctorate]] by [[ETH Zurich]] in 2013<ref>{{cite web|url=https://inf.ethz.ch/department/awards-rankings/honorary-doctors.html|title=Honorary doctors|publisher=ETH Zurich Department of Computer Science|access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref> and by the [[University of Waterloo]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/combinatorics-and-optimization/news/noga-alon-be-awarded-honorary-doctorate|title=Noga Alon to be awarded an Honorary Doctorate|publisher=University of Waterloo Department of Combinatorics and Optimization|date=2 June 2015|access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref>

In addition, Alon has been a member of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]] since 1997.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.academy.ac.il/Index2/Entry.aspx?nodeId=809&entryId=18227|title=Noga Alon|publisher=Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities|work=Members|access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref> He was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2008.<ref name=ae>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Alon_Noga|title=Noga Alon|publisher=Academia Europaea|work=Members|access-date=2023-05-05}}</ref> In 2015 he was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2015-11-16}}.</ref> In 2017 he became a [[Fellow of the Association for Computing Machinery]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=ACM Recognizes New Fellows|journal=[[Communications of the ACM]]|date=March 2017|volume=60|issue=3|page=23|doi=10.1145/3039921|s2cid=31701275 |last1=Cacm Staff }}.</ref> In 2019 he was named an honorary member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://physics.tau.ac.il/nogaalon|title=Prof. Noga Alon has been elected an Honorary member of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences|date=8 September 2019|work=School of Mathematical Sciences Newsroom|publisher=Tel Aviv University|access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref>

In 2024, Alon gave the opening plenary talk on "Distance problems for typical norms" at the 33rd Cumberland Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory, and Computing at [[Mississippi State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2024 |title=Conference Program |url=https://www.math.msstate.edu/sites/www.math.msstate.edu/files/inline-files/Conference%20program.pdf |access-date=10 August 2025 |website=MS State}}</ref>
